title: Conditional Sentences: First Practice — Quiz 78
content:
## Conditional Sentences: First Practice

Choose the correct verb forms in conditional sentences.

### Lesson focus

1. If you ___ time, time will waste you. (waste / will waste)
2. She will be ill if she ___ all that. (eat / eats)
3. If man ___, he can do wonders. (determines / will determine)
4. If you ___ late, you won't get a seat. (are / will be)

### Understand the pattern

The first conditional commonly combines if + present simple with will + base verb for a possible future result. A modal such as can may replace will when the result concerns ability or possibility. Do not normally add will to the if-clause in this pattern.

### Worked answers and explanation

1. waste
2. eats
3. determines
4. are

In 2, she requires the third-person singular eats. In 4, the future result is won't get, but the conditional clause uses present are. The exercise's literary wording 'If man determines' means if a person resolves to act.

### Try another

Complete: If Ravi ___ early, he will find a seat. (arrive)

### Suggested answer

Arrives. Present simple belongs in the if-clause, and the singular subject Ravi needs the -s form.
